The municipal sources establish an offshore naval action, followed by Jundō-maru grounding in the shallows, but provide no georeferenced engagement point. The preserved date 13 July 1868 corresponds to Keio 4, fifth month, day 24; the municipal museum is a repository of recovered material, not the battle position.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The rejected point [138.77022222222223,37.64497222222222] belongs to the linked former municipality Q7701513. Neither the town centre, the present harbour centre nor the museum location is a documented position of the ships. Remove coordinates; geographic uncertainty is unresolved and no precision is asserted.

inclusionReview.note: Teradomari is individually included as the naval action outside Teradomari harbour on 13 July 1868, within but distinct from the broader Hokuetsu fighting. Nagaoka City documents the attack on the anchored shogunate transport Jundō-maru and its grounding and destruction, dated Keio 4, fifth month, day 24. The cited Niigata University paper independently pairs that traditional date with 13 July 1868. This does not promote the broad naval-warfare class. The linked former municipality supplies no engagement position: its inherited point is explicitly withdrawn in the companion metadata review. No complete opposing strengths or losses are added.
